positions.hcc: Ablation and selected Y90 radiation segmentectomy can both have curative intent. Choose by tumor size, location, liver reserve, achievable ablation margin or segmental dosimetry. Ablation has more randomized comparative evidence. Y90 versus ablation studies are mainly observational. Y90 is associated with less waitlist dropout than TACE in registry analyses, but no dedicated randomized comparison establishes a transplant or survival advantage.
positions.crlm: Resection and ablation remain options for complete clearance of suitable liver disease. HAI plus systemic therapy can support conversion or selected perioperative treatment. Matched HAI–Y90 cohorts favor HAI after fewer prior chemotherapy lines, with substantial center and treatment-selection confounding. HAI has not been shown to replace ablation for small ablatable metastases. Reassess complete local clearance after response.
positions.icca: Selected liver-confined unresectable iCCA may receive HAI or other liver-directed treatment in an experienced multidisciplinary program. HAI comparisons with TACE, chemotherapy or resection are nonrandomized and do not establish a universal ranking. No strong direct HAI–ablation or HAI–Y90 comparison was identified. Multifocal-study results do not distinguish satellites from intrahepatic metastases or expand transplant criteria.
positions.pcca: HAIC remains investigational for primary pCCA. A prospective nonrandomized study after biliary drainage reported longer survival with HAIC than drainage plus best supportive care, but did not compare modern systemic therapy or establish a transplant-bridging role. It does not replace a protocol neoadjuvant regimen or alter transplant eligibility.
positions.nelm: TAE, TACE and Y90 are selected for disease control or symptom relief according to tumor biology, liver burden, arterial anatomy and treatment sequence. A very small randomized TAE–Y90 pilot and discordant retrospective comparisons do not establish a preferred modality for survival. Consider delayed hepatic toxicity, particularly with extensive treatment and long anticipated survival. HAI has no established routine role.

studies.population: Solitary treatment-naïve HCC ≤4 cm; 68 patients, 24 matched pairs. RS versus MWA.
studies.result: Mean target-tumor PFS 57.8 versus 38.6 months (p=0.005); mean OS 59.0 versus 44.3 months (p=0.203).
studies.caution: Small matched cohorts; RS often selected for anatomy unsuitable for MWA. These are mean survival times, not medians. No proven OS superiority or equivalence.
studies.author: Arndt L
studies.title: Evaluation of Medium-Term Efficacy of Y90 Radiation Segmentectomy vs Percutaneous Microwave Ablation in Patients with Solitary Surgically Unresectable < 4 cm Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Propensity Score Matched Study.

studies.population: Solitary AJCC stage I HCC ≤4 cm; resin RS 20 versus MWA 40. RS tumors were larger.
studies.result: Main-text CR 85% versus 82.5%; adjusted PFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.20–1.51), OS HR 1.38 (0.30–6.34).
studies.caution: No significant PFS/OS difference. Anatomy determined treatment; deaths within 1 month excluded. Abstract CR differs from main text; main-text denominator used. No equivalence conclusion.
studies.author: Abdalla O
studies.title: A retrospective study on the outcomes of yttrium-90 radiation segmentectomy with resin microspheres compared to microwave ablation for early primary hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: Solitary HCC ≤3 cm; RS 41 versus TACE plus MWA 80 before matching.
studies.result: After matching: no significant difference in CR (p=0.94), time to progression (p=0.83), or OS (p>0.99).
studies.caution: Comparator is TACE plus MWA, not MWA alone. Selection bias and limited power; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
studies.author: Biederman DM
studies.title: Radiation Segmentectomy versus TACE Combined with Microwave Ablation for Unresectable Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma Up to 3 cm: A Propensity Score Matching Study.

studies.population: Solitary unresectable HCC ≥3 cm; TARE versus DEB-TACE plus ablation; 19 matched pairs.
studies.result: DCR 94.7% versus 100%; locoregional sessions 1.3 versus 1.9 (p=0.02). No significant survival, PFS or transplant-rate difference.
studies.caution: Combined comparator; small selected cohorts. Results do not show that TARE is superior to ablation alone.
studies.author: Yu Q
studies.title: Transarterial Radioembolization versus Transarterial Chemoembolization Plus Percutaneous Ablation for Unresectable, Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma of ≥3 cm: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.

studies.population: 53 transplanted patients; RS 28 versus TACE-MWA 25; 40 tumors per group, HCC ≤5 cm.
studies.result: Mean pathologic tumor necrosis 83.6% versus 79.0% (p=0.484); treatment modality was not independently associated with complete necrosis.
studies.caution: Transplanted patients only; cannot assess waitlist dropout. Complete-necrosis percentages have inconsistent denominators in Table 2 and are omitted. Most RS doses preceded current high-dose practice.
studies.author: Yu Q
studies.title: Radiation Segmentectomy versus Combined Chemoembolization plus Microwave Ablation: Histopathologic Tumor Necrosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Measuring up to 5 cm.

studies.population: Solitary HCC ≤8 cm; RS 57 versus resection 66.
studies.result: Target progression 5% versus 8%; adjusted overall-progression HR 1.16 (95% CI 0.51–2.63). Median OS not reached in either group.
studies.caution: Propensity distributions were too dissimilar to match. Different surgical candidacy and liver function prevent a claim of equivalence to resection.
studies.author: De la Garza-Ramos C
studies.title: Radiation Segmentectomy for the Treatment of Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Outcomes Compared with Those of Surgical Resection.

studies.population: UNOS T3 HCC; 43 TARE versus 43 TACE patients.
studies.result: Downstaging to T2: Y90 25/43 (58%) versus TACE 11/35 (31%), p=0.023. The 61% versus 37% figures describe partial response.
studies.caution: Retrospective. Eight TACE patients lacked follow-up imaging and were excluded from response analyses. Downstaging measured the whole lesion, including necrotic tissue; this is not the current viable-tumor method.
studies.author: Lewandowski RJ
studies.title: A comparative analysis of transarterial downstaging for hepatocellular carcinoma: chemoembolization versus radioembolization.

studies.population: 31,609 US HCC transplant candidates, 2003–2018; 24,145 received LRT.
studies.result: IPTW-adjusted dropout sHR versus TACE: radioembolization 0.85 (95% CI 0.81–0.89); thermal ablation 0.95 (0.91–0.99).
studies.caution: Observational first-treatment comparison, with later treatments allowed. Center, era and patient selection remain confounders. Registry cohorts overlap with later studies.
studies.author: Kwong AJ
studies.title: National Trends and Waitlist Outcomes of Locoregional Therapy Among Liver Transplant Candidates With Hepatocellular Carcinoma in the United States.

studies.population: 8,367 OPTN candidates, 2016–2024; sole modality TARE 2,895 versus TACE 5,472.
studies.result: Death/too-sick dropout sHR 0.83 (95% CI 0.74–0.93); complete-necrosis aOR 2.24 (1.88–2.67).
studies.caution: No significant adjusted OS, post-LT OS or recurrence difference. Switching/mixed LRT and LDLT excluded; overlaps Kim registry population. Final issue 2026, online 2025.
studies.author: Fakhoury B
studies.title: Evolving trends and comparative outcomes of bridging transarterial locoregional therapy in liver transplant candidates with hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 5,677 HCC-exception candidates, 2019–2024; first-line TARE versus TACE.
studies.result: Weighted cause-specific dropout HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.69–0.89); 2-year dropout 14.2% versus 19.0%. One LRT only: 80.6% versus 57.8%.
studies.caution: Observational registry association; both-modality recipients excluded from the primary analysis. Treatment details and selection remain incompletely measured. No proven post-transplant survival advantage.
studies.author: Kim NG
studies.title: Yttrium-90 radioembolization is associated with a lower risk of liver transplant waitlist dropout than chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: MERITS-LT: 326 within UNOS-DS and 190 all-comers beyond UNOS-DS; 2015–2023.
studies.result: In the all-comers subgroup, 2-year successful downstaging was 74% with initial Y90 versus 65% with TACE (p<0.001).
studies.caution: Treatment was not randomized; subgroup finding does not expand allocation criteria. Overlaps earlier MERITS-LT enrollment. Earlier within-UNOS-DS study found no significant modality difference.
studies.author: Xu E
studies.title: Downstaging of hepatocellular carcinoma before liver transplantation: Results from a national multicenter prospective cohort study.

studies.population: 172 transplanted patients: Y90 93 versus TACE 79.
studies.result: Post-LT recurrence 9% versus 8%; RFS and OS did not differ significantly.
studies.caution: Only recipients were analyzed. This cannot establish equivalent bridging success or compare dropout before transplantation.
studies.author: Gabr A
studies.title: Comparative study of post-transplant outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with chemoembolization or radioembolization.

studies.population: 131 recipients: Y90 44 versus TACE 87. Within Milan initially: 20.5% versus 65.5%.
studies.result: Post-LT recurrence 23% versus 11% (p=0.1224); no significant survival difference.
studies.caution: Major baseline imbalance; pre-LT dropouts (6 Y90, 8 TACE) excluded. Recipient outcomes do not answer the waitlist-dropout question.
studies.author: Benkö T
studies.title: Bridging treatment prior to liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma: radioembolization or transarterial chemoembolization?

studies.population: 60 recipients; 79 treatments across SBRT, TACE, RFA and Y90; only 9 Y90 and 9 RFA treatments.
studies.result: Complete pathologic response was reported in 75% after Y90 and 60% after RFA among evaluable explants.
studies.caution: Very small, unequal evaluable groups, mixed treatments and recipient selection; illustrative pathology results, not a modality ranking or dropout comparison.
studies.author: Mohamed M
studies.title: Comparison of outcomes between SBRT, yttrium-90 radioembolization, transarterial chemoembolization, and radiofrequency ablation as bridge to transplant for hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: SEER 2004–2011; 189 unresectable HCC patients, SIRT 77 versus coded SBRT 112.
studies.result: Adjusted OS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.49–1.07) for SIRT versus SBRT; no significant difference.
studies.caution: Older registry radiation coding and missing liver-function/dosimetry details limit applicability to modern RS versus SBRT. No equivalence conclusion.
studies.author: Oladeru OT
studies.title: Conformal external beam radiation or selective internal radiation therapy-a comparison of treatment outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 28 unresectable HCC patients: single-session SIRT 13 versus repeated TACE 15.
studies.result: DCR 76.9% versus 73.3%; no significant difference in 12-week health-related quality of life.
studies.caution: Safety/QoL pilot, not powered for survival or transplant endpoints. Complements, rather than confirms, PREMIERE and TRACE.
studies.author: Kolligs FT
studies.title: Pilot randomized trial of selective internal radiation therapy vs. chemoembolization in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 24 predominantly BCLC-B HCC patients: SIRT versus DEB-TACE, 12 per arm.
studies.result: Median PFS 180 versus 216 days; OS 592 versus 788 days; neither difference significant.
studies.caution: Four liver-failure deaths occurred after SIRT. Small trial with older delivery/dosimetry; no class-wide Y90 survival advantage.
studies.author: Pitton MB
studies.title: Randomized comparison of selective internal radiotherapy (SIRT) versus drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 70 early HCC patients: cisplatin HAIC before RFA versus RFA alone, 35 per arm.
studies.caution: Primary RFS endpoint was not significant. A secondary distant-intrahepatic recurrence signal does not establish routine HAIC addition or HAIC as a replacement for ablation.
studies.author: Oyama A
studies.title: Randomized controlled study to examine the efficacy of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy with cisplatin before radiofrequency ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 228 HCC patients with tumors >5 cm: HAIC followed by ablation 93 versus HAIC alone 135.
studies.result: Reported 2-year OS: 74.3% versus 27.7%. IPTW and 6-month landmark analyses favored HAIC followed by ablation.
studies.caution: Selected HAIC responders; substantial selection bias. Reported survival medians conflict with Results/Figure 2 and are omitted. Tests adding ablation after HAIC, not replacing ablation with HAIC.
studies.author: You H
studies.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy and sequential ablation treatment in large hepatocellular carcinoma.

studies.population: 206 advanced HCC patients; low-dose cisplatin/5-FU HAIC plus sorafenib versus sorafenib.
studies.caution: Negative OS trial. Regimen differs from FOLFOX-HAIC trials; increased hematologic toxicity. Do not generalize a benefit across all HAIC regimens.
studies.author: Kudo M
studies.title: Sorafenib plus low-dose cisplatin and fluorouracil hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus sorafenib alone in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (SILIUS): a randomised, open label, phase 3 trial.

studies.population: 708 HAI versus 481 TARE patients; matched within prior systemic-therapy lines.
studies.result: TARE-versus-HAI mortality HR: 1 prior line 1.46 (95% CI 1.02–2.08); 2 lines 1.96 (1.32–2.89); 3–4 lines 0.88 (0.57–1.35).
studies.caution: HAI came from one high-volume center, TARE from five others. More subsequent systemic therapy/resection after HAI; treatment and center effects cannot be separated. Not a comparison with ablation.
studies.author: Saadat LV
studies.title: Hepatic Artery Infusion Chemotherapy Compared to Transarterial Radioembolization For Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases.

studies.population: 97 pretreated liver-only CRLM patients: HAI 48 versus Y90 49, with modern systemic therapy.
studies.result: Median OS from isolated unresectable diagnosis: 31.2 versus 16.3 months (p<0.001). From initial stage IV diagnosis: 34.4 versus 32.0 months (p=0.291).
studies.caution: Retrospective, 97 patients. Survival time origin changes the apparent comparison; treatment timing, subsequent therapy and selection limit causal interpretation.
studies.author: Dhir M
studies.title: Effectiveness of Hepatic Artery Infusion (HAI) Versus Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (Y90) for Pretreated Isolated Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases (IU-CRCLM).

studies.population: 74 patients with bilobar unresectable CRLM: Y90 plus regional FUDR versus regional FUDR alone.
studies.result: Tumor-volume response 50% versus 24% (p=0.03); liver progression was delayed.
studies.caution: Tests adding Y90 to HAI, not Y90 versus HAI alone. Older chemotherapy era; no established overall-survival benefit. Not evidence against ablation of small lesions.
studies.author: Gray B
studies.title: Randomised trial of SIR-Spheres plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone for treating patients with liver metastases from primary large bowel cancer.

studies.population: 202 CRLM patients; 44 matched pairs, DEB-TACE versus TARE.
studies.result: Adjusted OS association for DEB-TACE: HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.54–1.65), p=0.83; toxicity trend 27% versus 9.1%, p=0.057.
studies.caution: No significant survival difference; baseline burden and extrahepatic disease varied. Not an equivalence trial.
studies.author: Mokkarala M
studies.title: Comparison of Response and Outcomes of Drug-eluting Bead Chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) Versus Radioembolization (TARE) for Patients With Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases.

studies.population: Persistently unresectable liver-only CRLM after systemic induction; 11 HAI-oxaliplatin plus systemic versus 9 systemic alone randomized.
studies.result: Conversion to resection/ablation 7/11 (64%) versus 2/9 (22%), p=0.09; PFS 12.6 versus 4.37 months.
studies.caution: Very small, early-closed trial; conversion endpoint not significant. Supports further study, not a confirmed conversion advantage or direct comparison against ablation.
studies.author: Boilève A
studies.title: Treatment Intensification with Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy in Patients with Liver-Only Colorectal Metastases Still Unresectable After Systemic Induction Chemotherapy: Exploratory Findings From a Prematurely Closed Multicenter Randomized Phase II Study: SULTAN UCGI 30/PRODIGE 53 (NCT03164655).

studies.population: 92 randomized after CRLM surgery; modified ITT 77, HAI-FUDR plus systemic 38 versus systemic 39.
studies.result: 3-year RFS 31.4% versus 34.4%, p=0.28.
studies.caution: Stopped for FUDR supply shortage; primary endpoint negative. Exploratory early-RFS/subgroup signals do not establish routine postoperative HAI.
studies.author: Wang DS
studies.title: Safety and efficacy of adjuvant FOLFOX/FOLFIRI with versus without hepatic arterial infusion of floxuridine in patients following colorectal cancer liver metastasectomy (HARVEST trial): A randomized controlled trial.

studies.population: 99 patients after resection/ablation of ≥4 CRLM: HAI-oxaliplatin 50 versus IV oxaliplatin 49, both with IV LV5FU2.
studies.result: Hepatic RFS 25 versus 12 months, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.40–0.99); OS HR 0.61 (0.33–1.12), not significant. Grade 3–4 AEs 58% versus 32%.
studies.caution: Selected adjuvant setting after complete local treatment of ≥4 CRLM. Phase II design amended before database lock; early closure and immature OS limit certainty. Oxaliplatin infusion is not FUDR pump therapy.
studies.author: Gelli M
studies.title: Postoperative Hepatic Arterial Infusion With Oxaliplatin After Surgery of Four or More Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Randomized Phase II Trial.

studies.population: 1–3 CRLM, each ≤4 cm and suitable for both treatments; 100 randomized, 92 modified ITT.
studies.result: 1-year freedom from local progression: MWA 77.7% versus SBRT 83.0%; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.43–1.74), p=0.70. Grade ≥2 toxicity 25% versus 3%.
studies.caution: No demonstrated local-control difference; wide CI and postrandomization exclusions. No survival/noninferiority claim. Grade ≥3 toxicity occurred only after MWA, including one treatment-related death.
studies.author: Risumlund SL
studies.title: Microwave ablation versus stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic colorectal liver metastases (LAVA-CRLM): a prospective, randomised, phase II trial.

studies.population: 126 unresectable iCCA patients; mFOLFOX-HAIC versus TACE.
studies.result: 1-year OS 60.2% versus 42.9%; 2-year OS 38.7% versus 29.4% (OS comparison p=0.028). PFS did not differ significantly.
studies.caution: Nonrandomized, regional catheter regimen. Does not establish pump-FUDR superiority or replace contemporary systemic therapy.
studies.author: Cai Z
studies.title: Survival Comparisons of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy With mFOLFOX and Transarterial Chemoembolization in Patients With Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.

studies.population: 181 patients: HAIC 24, conventional TACE 73, DEB-TACE 84.
studies.result: HAIC versus conventional TACE median OS 10.3 versus 5.1 months (p=0.0042); no significant HAIC-versus-DEB-TACE difference reported.
studies.caution: Very small HAIC cohort; treatment selection and TACE formulation matter. Do not generalize the comparison to all arterial therapy.
studies.author: Zhang Y
studies.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus transarterial chemoembolization in patients with unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.

studies.population: 319 multifocal iCCA patients: unresectable HAIP-FUDR 141 versus resection 178 across different centers/eras.
studies.result: Median OS 20.3 versus 18.9 months; adjusted HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.55–1.03), p=0.07.
studies.caution: HAIP patients had substantially more bilobar/multifocal disease. Not an equivalence trial or reason to deny resection to an otherwise suitable patient; does not distinguish all satellites from metastases.
studies.author: Franssen S
studies.title: Comparison of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy vs Resection for Patients With Multifocal Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.

studies.population: 268 liver-confined unresectable iCCA patients: HAIP ± systemic 192 versus gemcitabine/cisplatin 76.
studies.result: Median OS 27.7 versus 11.8 months; approximately one third of HAIP patients alive at 3 years.
studies.caution: Nonrandomized center, era and treatment-line differences; 71.9% of HAIP patients also received systemic treatment. Comparator predates current chemoimmunotherapy; not HAI versus Y90 or ablation.
studies.author: Franssen S
studies.title: Gemcitabine with Cisplatin Versus Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy for Liver-Confined Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.

studies.population: 40 unresectable iCCA patients: Y90 25 versus chemoembolization 15.
studies.result: Table 3 disease control: Y90 12/25 (48%) versus chemoembolization 7/15 (47%); no significant difference. Survival was not assessed.
studies.caution: Small retrospective cohort. Abstract and body percentages conflict; counts from Table 3 are used. Missing response status and treatment crossover limit comparison.
studies.author: Akinwande O
studies.title: Chemoembolization versus radioembolization for the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in a single institution image-based efficacy and comparative toxicity.

studies.population: Main-text analysis: SBRT 27, chemoradiation 54, TARE 60; nonmetastatic node-negative unresected iCCA.
studies.result: Adjusted OS HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.21–0.84) for SBRT versus TARE.
studies.caution: TARE tumors were larger/more often multifocal or vascular-invasive. Strong selection bias and abstract/main-text cohort-count discrepancy; not causal superiority or equivalent treatment eligibility.
studies.author: Sebastian NT
studies.title: Stereotactic body radiation therapy is associated with improved overall survival compared to chemoradiation or radioembolization in the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

studies.population: 127 advanced pCCA patients after biliary drainage: catheter HAIC 63 versus best supportive care 64; preserved reserve, no distant/N2 disease.
studies.result: Median OS 17.63 versus 6.10 months.
studies.caution: Patient preference/clinical selection; no contemporary systemic-therapy comparator. Hypothesis-generating disease-control evidence, not established standard, cure, or a transplant-bridging protocol.
studies.author: Dai Y
studies.title: Biliary drainage plus hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus biliary drainage plus best supportive care for advanced perihilar cholangiocarcinoma in China: a prospective multicentre non-randomised controlled study.

studies.population: 11 small-intestinal NET patients: Y90 6 versus bland embolization 5.
studies.result: 3-month RECIST response 0/6 versus 5/5 (p=0.0022); 6-month response 2/6 versus 4/5, not significant.
studies.caution: Tiny study; response timing differs after radiation. No survival ranking and no extrapolation to all NET primaries.
studies.author: Elf AK
studies.title: Radioembolization Versus Bland Embolization for Hepatic Metastases from Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors: Short-Term Results of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

studies.population: 248 NELM patients: TARE 51 versus TACE 197.
studies.result: Initial DCR 83% versus 96% (p<0.01); no significant OS or PFS difference. TARE was usually outpatient.
studies.caution: Nonrandomized baseline and treatment-selection differences. Does not prove equivalence; treatment burden and delayed toxicity also matter.
studies.author: Egger ME
studies.title: Transarterial Chemoembolization vs Radioembolization for Neuroendocrine Liver Metastases: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.

studies.population: 192 GEP-NET patients: cTACE 122, DEB-TACE 26, Y90 44.
studies.result: Propensity-weighted median OS: cTACE versus Y90 34.0 versus 22.9 months (p=0.032); cTACE versus DEB-TACE 33.8 versus 23.4 months (p=0.04).
studies.caution: Retrospective pairwise weighting across a long treatment era. These adjusted medians differ from the unadjusted three-group medians. Residual confounding prevents a definitive modality ranking.
studies.author: Do Minh D
studies.title: Intra-arterial therapy of neuroendocrine tumour liver metastases: comparing conventional TACE, drug-eluting beads TACE and yttrium-90 radioembolisation as treatment options using a propensity score analysis model.

studies.population: NELM patients surviving ≥1 year: TACE 63 versus TARE 28; chronic grade ≥3 hepatic toxicity beginning ≥6 months after treatment.
studies.result: Chronic hepatic toxicity: 22% versus 29%. Injury attributed solely to embolotherapy: 3% versus 14% (p=0.07), with more clinical decompensation after TARE.
studies.caution: Retrospective survivor-selected cohort. Most TACE toxicities coincided with progression. This cannot estimate toxicity in all treated patients or establish equivalent safety.
studies.author: Currie BM
studies.title: Chronic Hepatotoxicity in Patients with Metastatic Neuroendocrine Tumor: Transarterial Chemoembolization versus Transarterial Radioembolization.

studies.population: 30 lung-carcinoid patients, 53 primary embolization procedures; Y90 versus bland TAE.
studies.result: Local progression-free survival 30.57 versus 13.9 months (p=0.01); OS 43.5 versus 40.6 months (p=0.49).
studies.caution: Primary-specific, small retrospective study with repeated procedures and systemic-treatment confounding; not generalizable to all NELM.
studies.author: Yuan G
studies.title: Yttrium-90 Radioembolization Versus Transarterial Embolization for Lung Carcinoid Hepatic Metastasis.
